recommendation_summary: Right now: drop Kafka, CQRS and Redis, and change the existing endpoint to use a PostgreSQL COUNT(*) with the unpaid filter, so it stops building invoice objects. It also says to check the query plan and latency under representative load and to add an index only if the evidence calls for it. It offers no optional new services, and request-time freshness is kept.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need an unpaid-invoice count within one second that reflects committed invoices at request time.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, CQRS projection, and Redis for this count; approved budget and peer adoption do not establish a need.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint retrieves rows and constructs objects just to count them.
labels.Checked myself: Only your supplied description; performance and query plans remain unverified.

note: The reply puts all four record lines before an aggregate-query recommendation, rejects the named stack, and is honest about what it did not verify.
